blocks.html:
Drive out of Phuket Town along Thepkrasattri Road toward Rassada subdistrict and you'll come across a plain shophouse restaurant called "Ton Mayom." The name wasn't picked to sound catchy — it comes from an actual old mayom (star gooseberry) tree the restaurant sits under, in its shade. The owners are Khun Hua and Khun Ood, two siblings as close as best friends, who opened the place together with no fancy concept at all — just one thing they were confident about: real, full-flavored Southern Thai food the way Southern Thai people actually eat it, without toning down the spice or softening the taste for tourists. That honesty to the region's flavor is exactly what earned it a Bib Gourmand from MICHELIN, and the recognition has held continuously through the 2026 guide.

Ton Mayom's menu is short and tight — not hundreds of dishes to pick through, because they only make what they can do well. The dish MICHELIN singles out as the star is the crispy fried local fish topped with fragrant Southern curry paste: fish fried until crisp, then topped with Southern curry paste stir-fried until the whole restaurant smells of it, eaten with hot steamed rice — about as straightforward a pleasure as it gets. Another dish that belongs on the table is the sour curry with sea bass and coconut shoots, a Southern-style sour curry that leads with tang, follows with heat, turns a bright yellow from turmeric, and gets sweet crunch from tender young coconut shoots that balance out the intensity of the broth. Round it out with stir-fried prawns with shrimp paste and sataw beans, a Southern classic that tests a cook's skill immediately — the shrimp paste has to smell fragrant, not fishy, and the sataw beans need to stay crunchy without turning too bitter and green-tasting.

What's worth thinking about is that Phuket is an island packed with premium restaurants and Baba-style eateries in the old town where tourists line up to take photos. Ton Mayom lives in a completely different world from that picture. It's a place locals have quietly eaten at for years, long before MICHELIN put a pin on it and turned into a spot with queues stretching from late morning into the afternoon. If you want to know what real, unpretentious home-style Southern Thai cooking tastes like, a short drive out of town gets you the answer — at prices you can afford any day, not just for a special occasion. That's the real weight behind this Bib Gourmand.

blocks.name: Ton Mayom
blocks.descHtml:
Ton Mayom is priced at the budget-friendly tier under MICHELIN's own symbol (฿), so you can eat well without overthinking the bill. The restaurant is open daily 08:00–20:00, closed every Wednesday. It doesn't take table bookings — walk-in only — but if you want to pre-order food or check whether it's open, call +66 94 429 2265. Bring cash, since it's cash only.

The restaurant sits on Thepkrasattri Road, on the outbound side leaving Phuket Town, in Rassada subdistrict on the edge of town. Driving or riding a motorbike is the easiest way there since it isn't in a walkable tourist area. The best times to go are before 11:00 or after the lunch rush, because since earning its MICHELIN listing the restaurant has had queues running from late morning into the afternoon, especially at lunch when it's busiest. Dress is casual — it's a shophouse restaurant with a homey feel, good either as a stop before heading up to the island's northern side or on the way back into town from the airport.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at Ton Mayom?
faq.a: No table bookings — walk-in only. You can call ahead to ask questions or pre-order food at +66 94 429 2265, and the restaurant is cash only, so bring enough

faq.q: How much should I budget for a meal at Ton Mayom?
faq.a: It's a budget-friendly restaurant under MICHELIN's ฿ symbol — priced like a local Southern Thai restaurant you could eat at every day, not a special-occasion splurge. Order several dishes to share and it's still easy on the wallet

faq.q: What should I order at Ton Mayom?
faq.a: MICHELIN's pick is the crispy fried local fish topped with fragrant Southern curry paste, followed by sour curry with sea bass and coconut shoots, and stir-fried prawns with shrimp paste and sataw beans. Come ready for real Southern Thai heat — it isn't toned down

faq.q: What time does it open, and when's the queue shortest?
faq.a: Open 08:00–20:00, closed every Wednesday. The restaurant is on Thepkrasattri Road, outbound side leaving Phuket Town, in Rassada subdistrict. Since earning its MICHELIN listing, queues run from late morning into the afternoon — go before 11:00 or after the lunch rush for a shorter wait
